text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

An all-women panel choosing a woman over you — also a woman — gives you no sex-discrimination argument. Both finalists shared your sex, so the panel's composition explains nothing about the outcome. Raising it would read as grasping and would undermine the parts of your case that are genuinely strong.

Those parts are real: on paper you out-credential the appointee (completed PhD, six papers, four years teaching). The legitimate questions are whether "industry experience" was a weighted criterion in the published advertisement, and why your statutory/policy request for written reasons has gone unanswered for two weeks.

Send a dated follow-up citing the university's own appeal deadlines, request the scoring matrix, and keep your challenge on process and criteria.
